neutral_facts.value: The accused, a driver, was responsible for transporting a female victim who worked late hours at a company in Bengaluru. The victim left her office at 2:00 a.m. in a company-provided vehicle. The accused informed her that the vehicle on her usual route was unavailable and offered to transport her in his own vehicle. The victim sat in the accused's car. The victim's maternal uncle reported her missing, and her body was later recovered. The prosecution established that the accused committed rape, and the victim was found dead at the age of 28. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for the rest of his life. The high court did not review the case, and the supreme court modified the sentence to a fixed term of thirty years.

prosecution_argument.value: The State Government preferred an appeal for enhancement of the sentence, arguing that the Constitutional Courts are not powerless to impose modified sentences considering the gravity of the offence, the conduct of the accused and other relevant factors even though the death penalty has not been imposed.

defence_argument.value: The appellant contended that in view of the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench in the case of Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan & Ors., a modified sentence can be imposed only by the Constitutional Courts and not by the Sessions Courts. He also relied upon decisions showing that imposition of a modified sentence was made only in cases where the death penalty has been commuted.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the power to impose a modified punishment of providing any specific term of incarceration or till the end of the convict’s life as an alternative to death penalty can be exercised only by the High Court and the Supreme Court and not by any other inferior Court.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The Trial Court considered the appellant's age, family circumstances, and that this was his first offence as mitigating factors.

quotes.text: The Trial Court noted the fact that on the date of conviction, the age of the appellant was 27 years and he had a wife and small child as well as aged parents. Considering these factors along with the fact that this was the first offence committed by the appellant, the Trial Court found that the case was not falling in the category of the 'rarest of the rare' cases.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: The Court noted the brutal nature of the offence, the shock to the conscience of the Court, and the need to uphold public confidence in the legal system.

quotes.text: The Court, while considering the possibility of reformation of the accused, must note that showing undue leniency in such a brutal case will adversely affect the public confidence in the efficacy of the legal system.
